bullets: Nexus product strategy and roadmap. Prioritize the work that makes Nexus the durable connectivity layer across teams, namespaces, services, and AI systems.
Current execution. Drive completion of in-flight work such as the new Nexus developer experience, Standalone Nexus Operations, connector foundations, caller identity, rate limits…
Customer discovery and evidence. Stay close to design partners and strategic customers like Netflix, Duolingo, and Miro.
Developer and operator experience. Balance SDK ergonomics, schema-first contracts, codegen, service discovery, security, visibility, and control-plane needs.
Cross-functional launch and enablement. Make sure everyone in the company understands the problems Nexus solves and knows how to sell / deploy / support it.
Staff-level product ownership. You take an ambiguous strategic question and turn it into a roadmap and shipped outcomes with minimal direction. 8+ years in product management or…
Deep AI fluency. You are hands-on with the AI tooling landscape (eg, agent frameworks and SDKs, model providers, eval and observability tools) and you have an opinionated…
Ecosystem, platform, or partnerships product experience. You've owned integrations, a developer platform, or partner-facing products, not just end-user features.
GTM partnership instincts. You've worked hand-in-hand with Product Marketing, Sales, Solutions Architecture, and external partners to launch products and drive adoption, and you…
Technical literacy. You reason fluently about AI systems, and can hold your own in a design conversation with Staff engineers. You don't need to write production code.

roles.title: Senior Product Manager, Hybrid Platform & Deployment Models

bullets: Own supported self-hosted and hybrid deployment models , including clear positioning, lifecycle expectations, and customer outcomes.
Improve installation, configuration, upgrades, and operability so customers can run Temporal confidently in production across varied infrastructure.
Drive product direction for production readiness and operational tooling (observability, benchmarking, runbooks, diagnostics, upgrade safety).
Define strategy and requirements around database and storage choices , balancing operability, reliability, and customer constraints.
Own multi-region and multi-cloud topology capabilities for self-hosted environments, including performance and resilience tradeoffs.

roles.title: Staff Product Manager,  Cloud Namespace & Capacity

bullets: Own the full Cloud Namespace lifecycle for an operator using Temporal Cloud: understanding workload needs, provisioning and management flows, defining the right configuration…
Define and evolve differentiated Namespace offerings (e.g., higher/lower SLA, latency, durability, residency, and cost options) that are easy for customers to understand and trust.
Own throughput and capacity management for Namespaces (e.g., autoscaling, TRUs, reserved vs. elastic capacity, scheduling, visibility, limits, and quotas).
Drive operational policy and features (Namespace placement in deployment rings, replication, scaling) to deliver highly performant, reliable, and cost-effective service at massive…
Define and own Namespace SLOs and SLAs , including instrumentation and customer-facing communication of performance and reliability expectations.
Own the product strategy and roadmap for a focused Core Primitives charter
Translate customer, field, and open-source community signals into platform bets, deciding when to improve an existing primitive, introduce a new abstraction, change SDK/API…
Partner deeply with engineering to ship core behavior improvements across server, SDKs, and APIs, making Temporal easier to model with, operate, and trust in production
Define developer experience goals and success metrics before major investments, then validate, measure, and iterate with technical users
Set clear product boundaries and success criteria so developers, internal teams, and adjacent product areas know how Core Primitives should be used and extended
